note: Printed cello fingerings, SIGHT-READ from a scan (not extracted from a digital score). Read the caveats below before treating a number from this file as ground truth.
source: F. A. Kummer, Violoncellschule Op.60, ed. Hugo Becker (C. F. Peters), printed pages 14-16: Die Dur-Skalen and Die Moll-Skalen. Scan 600 ppi.
licence: PD. Kummer d.1879; Becker d.1941 -> PD since 2012. The fingerings are BECKER'S editorial layer, not Kummer's — an explicit reform edition, so they document early-20th-c technique.

provenance.method: Read by eye at native resolution, no OMR. Page 14 is DOUBLE-KEYED: its C-dur system was read independently by two readers who agreed on both fingering rows note for note. Pages 15 and 16 are SINGLE readings.
provenance.alignment_check: Every printed 0 was verified to land on C2/G2/D3/A3 and nothing else — 30 zeros on p14, 25 on p15, 31 on p16. This is the check that catches a digit row slipping against the noteheads, which is the failure mode that would otherwise look plausible and be wrong. p16 enforces it in its generator, which refuses to emit otherwise.
provenance.known_gaps: Source ABSENCES are recorded as null and must be SKIPPED, not scored: p14 A-dur and p15 A-moll do not print the upper row across the third octave (the octave-label boxes occupy that strip). Scoring nulls as misses would set the floor artificially low.

scoring.target: Use `finger` (upper row) where third_octave == false, and `alt` (lower row) where true. Becker's prose fixes this: 'vor der Hand nur im Umfang von 2 Oktaven, mit Benutzung des ueber den Noten stehenden Fingersatzes' — the upper row is the TWO-OCTAVE fingering, so it is not the intended target in the third octave.
scoring.floors: Per page, never pooled. These are three different plates read by different readers; averaging them hides a regression on one page behind a gain on another.
scoring.not_a_ceiling: One editor's fingering is one valid answer among several. The violin literature scores against ten annotators because professionals agree on the string (MRR ~.91) and disagree on the position (F1 ~.24-.31). Treat a drop as a bug and a rise as evidence, not a target to optimise.
